title: Manuel Manetta, the all-round player, at Captain Powell's
summary: Vincent recalls a regular job for Captain Powell and Manuel Manetta, who played any instrument, being made to play piano all night.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You know, her used to play with my other brother, too. Down where I was talking about the old accent. Who? She played with the name of the artist Louie. That's when, you know, her, Monty Minelli, you know? Yeah, I know.

She was playing piano down there. And then Monty Minelli, you know, when Monty Minelli was playing with that guy? Oh, yeah, sure. Yeah, we used to play out there for Captain Powell. That's right. That was a regular job we had out there. I remember one time. The first thing was on then, you know? Used to get plenty of homeboys and the lightning there, you know? You know, let's go ahead. He could go anyway with Captain Powell, man. I remember one time we went out to play out about the Art of Untyrone. Oh, yeah, yeah. And didn't have no piano. Yeah. And Manuel was with us then. Yeah. So Jack told Mangan he'd pat all night and he'd get paid. If he couldn't pat, he couldn't get paid. Mangan's hand got all sore that night. Yeah, I remember that night. Yeah, that's true. Mangan was playing soccer with us then. Mangan could play any kind of blowing, that's me. Klein it, corn it. Sometimes he'd put corn it with us. Two sharpies together. Yeah, two sharpies together. Ask him did he ever make any records? Did Mangan ever make any records? I can't remember. Man, he could play any kind of blues, like Clowness, Cornette. He'd play two trumpets, right? Yeah, two trumpets together.
